synopsis: The manufacturer needs a strategy and roadmap for predominantly virtual collision-mitigation validation, planned as an eleven-month first-of-a-kind programme under a hard deadline, with about seven months from October 2026 to April 2027 to prepare the capability [f6, f9396, f9400, f9402]. The four-month validation window cannot be compressed: integrated product validation starts at prototype arrival, but earlier work must establish a proven method so that the window becomes a confirmation and calibration campaign [f62, f10895, f11929]. Before mid-2027, the proposed preparation scope includes site geometry, material libraries, scenarios, machine kinematics, reference measurements, metrics, HIL interfaces and generic effect models; each work package should produce safety evidence, with traceable claim-to-requirement-to-scenario-to-test mapping as the first deliverable [f4973, f9398, f12193]. Schedule confidence remains limited: no published case proves the four-month schedule, reliable heavy-off-road setup durations and build-versus-buy staffing, timeline and cost figures are unavailable, and the October 2026 plan is an assessment rather than a documented case [f6398, f811, f8314, f892]. Modeling effort varies substantially—from hours for an energy or constant-deceleration model to months for detailed multibody modeling—while the on-road PEGASUS precedent lasted 42 months and produced a method, not an approval [f6427, f6457, f1543, f1546]. Planning should therefore include standards re-baselining before design freeze, owned supplier dependencies before architecture freeze, budgeted simulation-tool qualification, early independent-test booking with at least one re-test, and a restricted-scope alternative with stage gates [f2948, f10802, f10547, f5790, f11075].

relations.note: Both say the four-month window cannot shrink, but work can move earlier.
Both report PEGASUS's identical dates and 42-month duration.
Both distinguish prototype-triggered integrated validation from the earlier programme start.
Both report missing public off-highway build-versus-buy staffing, timeline and cost evidence.
Both report absent integration-effort benchmarks; engineer-weeks per connection remain unavailable.
Both state that no planning method has consistent outcome evidence.
Both report missing documented heavy-off-road setup durations rather than supplying completion estimates.
Both report missing published effort and cost figures for job-site environment construction.
The roadmap requirement adds new-capability scope and a hard deadline.
The eleven-month programme includes about seven months of capability preparation.
Moving work earlier makes the prototype window a confirmation and calibration campaign.
Lists the prerequisites that must precede prototype arrival.
Specifies traceability mapping as the first safety-evidence deliverable.
Tool qualification is budgeted work supporting simulation-based safety evidence.
Re-baselining must use ISO editions actually published.
Preparing material libraries requires creating the missing job-site material layer.
An unproven four-month schedule motivates restricted scope and stage gates.
Pre-committed stop and descope criteria support gated fallback planning.
